sections.heading: When It's Time to Stop Repairing
body: You've paid for a repair, and then another. The house heats unevenly, the furnace starts and stops, or the water heater leaves you with a cold shower halfway through.
An old heater doesn't fail in one dramatic moment. Parts wear, efficiency drops, and the repair bills begin to look like a down payment on a new one.
That's the point to ask for an install quote. We put in new furnaces and water heaters for Wichita homes, and we'll tell you what failed on yours so you can decide with the facts in front of you.

sections.heading: Furnace or Water Heater
body: Both are "heaters," and both are in our line of work.

**A furnace** warms the air that moves through your house. Gas furnaces carry a burner, an igniter, a blower and a heat exchanger. When the heat exchanger cracks, replacing the furnace is usually the answer, because that part can't be fixed safely.

**A water heater** keeps a tank of hot water ready, or heats it on demand. Tanks rust from the inside and collect sediment, especially in hard water, and a tank that has started to leak can't be repaired.
If you're not sure which one you need, call and tell us what's happening. Cold rooms point to the furnace, and cold showers point to the water heater.

sections.heading: Why the Install Matters as Much as the Unit
body: A good heater installed badly is still a bad heater. A furnace that's too big short-cycles and wears out early. One that's too small never catches up on a January night.

Venting is the part people don't see. A gas furnace or water heater has to send combustion gases outside, and a poor connection can put them in the house. A water heater that isn't connected and drained correctly can leak into a floor.
This is why installation shouldn't be a rush job. The unit has to match the house, and the work around it has to be done correctly.

sections.heading: When One Part Stops the Whole House
body: The fan outside has stopped. The unit hums and nothing moves. Or the furnace clicks, tries to light and gives up.
These failures feel like the end of a system. Often they're a single worn part: a capacitor, a fan motor, an igniter, a blower motor.
A system that has years left in it shouldn't be replaced because one component quit. That's what parts replacement is for.

sections.quote: My condenser fan motor went out on my A/C last night , I called my landlord this morning by 11:30am. My A/C was fixed and running better than ever. The technician was polite and very knowledgeable of the task he was doing.

sections.heading: The Parts That Fail Most
body: Moving parts wear out first, and the ones that work hardest wear fastest.
list: **Motors and fans.** The condenser fan outside and the blower inside run every time the system does. Bearings wear, and they stall.
**Capacitors and contactors.** These give motors their start-up jolt. A weak one makes a unit hum but not start.
**Igniters and sensors.** A furnace that clicks and quits is often failing here.
**Refrigerant lines and coils.** A leak lets refrigerant out, and cooling slowly fades. Topping it off without finding the leak just starts the clock again.
tail: Repairing the right part costs far less than replacing a system. Repairing the wrong part is how you pay twice.

We find the problem and explain it in plain terms, so you understand what broke, whether it can happen again and what the repair involves. A technician who knows the equipment can often name the cause with little digging.

sections.heading: Why a Leak Needs Repeat Attention
body: Refrigerant doesn't burn off like gasoline. If the level is low, there is a leak somewhere, and a slow leak can take more than one visit to chase down.
That's why it helps to have the same person every time. He knows what's already been tried, what was refilled and where he suspects the leak is.
It's also why the call is to Nate's own number, not a dispatcher who doesn't know your history.

sections.heading: Maintenance That Catches It Early
body: Most parts don't fail without warning. Filters clog, belts and bearings get noisy, coils collect dirt, and the system works harder until something gives.
We do maintenance on heating and cooling equipment, so small problems are found before they become a dead system on the hottest or coldest day of the year.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace
body: A part is the right answer when the rest of the system is in decent shape. It's the wrong answer when the unit is old and failing in several places, or when the compressor or heat exchanger has gone.

We'll tell you which you're facing. If replacement makes sense, we install furnaces, water heaters and air conditioners too, and our [heater installation page](/heater-installation-wichita-ks/) explains how that goes.
